title: Constitutive sensitivity of the high-loading thermal pass and post-glass ranking
question: How does independent scaling of SAR and specimen volumetric heat capacity affect the two schedule decisions in the clamped 1.83 mg Fe/mL phantom?
method: Frozen hypothetical 3 by 3 source/capacity grid, fixed transition probes, adiabatic finite-volume midpoint RK2, 0.75 mm discovery and paired 0.5 mm time refinement. Whole-specimen and myocardial screens computed separately.
result: Across the three discovery capacity levels the flat schedule failed at SAR/capacity ratio 0.992 and passed at 0.996. Nominal-capacity fine-grid checks reproduced this bracket. The ramp retained the higher post-glass minimum across all nine discovery settings and all paired refinements.
limitations: Hypothetical coherent scalar perturbations, finite deterministic sampling and no measured confidence bounds.
Synthetic geometry, adiabatic wall exterior, fixed loading and clamped low-temperature SAR.
Some weak-heating voxels did not complete the diagnostic transit. Spatial discretization affects terminal extrema.
Thermal model only. No human expert review, population inference or biological outcome validation.
